search-start: Let's look for {key}. We always start at the root.
compare-equal: {key} is right here in this node.
compare-less: {key} < {upper}, so follow the yarn to the leftmost child.
compare-greater: {key} > {lower}, so follow the yarn right to the last child.
compare-between: {key} is between {lower} and {upper}, so take the child in between.
compare-leaf: This is a leaf, so the search stops here. {key} belongs in this node.
not-found: We reached a leaf without finding {key}, so it is not in the tree.
empty-tree: The tree is empty, so there is nothing to search yet.
insert-start: Let's insert {key}. First we find the leaf where it belongs.
create-root: The tree was empty, so {key} becomes the root.
duplicate: {key} is already in the tree. B-trees here keep each key once, so nothing changes.
insert-key: {key} goes into the leaf in sorted order. The leaf now holds {size} of {max} keys, so it fits.
insert-key-full: {key} goes into the leaf in sorted order, but now it holds {size} keys and only has room for {max}.
overflow: This node is full, so the middle key, {median}, moves up to the parent.
split: Snap! The node splits around {median}: [{left}] stays on the left and [{right}] goes right.
promote: {median} hops up into the parent. The parent holds {size} of {max} keys, so we stop.
promote-overflow: {median} hops up into the parent, but now the parent overflows too ({size} keys). Split again!
new-root: The root split, so {median} becomes a new root. The tree just grew one level taller, at the top.
insert-done: Done. Every leaf is still on the same level.
delete-start: Let's delete {key}. First we find it.
delete-not-found: {key} is not in the tree, so there is nothing to delete.
predecessor-descend: {key} is in an internal node. We walk down to the largest key on its left side.
replace-predecessor: {pred} replaces {key}, and is removed from its leaf instead.
underflow: This node now holds {size} key(s), fewer than the minimum of {min}.
borrow-left: The left sibling can spare a key: {down} comes down from the parent and {up} moves up.
borrow-right: The right sibling can spare a key: {down} comes down from the parent and {up} moves up.
merge: No sibling can spare a key, so we merge with one, pulling {separator} down: [{keys}].
shrink-root: The root ran out of keys, so its only child becomes the new root. The tree is one level shorter.
tree-empty: That was the last key. The tree is empty.
delete-done: Done. The tree is a valid B-tree again.
